b_title: How to Live Well — A Formally Verified Guide
one_line: Both ask 'how should one live?': A (philosophy2) offers a plural, first-person toolkit in which you discover/create your own philosophy across moods, dilemmas and a dozen traditions; B (good.html) builds a single axiomatic, machine-verified ethics whose nine principles form a sheaf over Self/Other/Community that glues into a global section 'good_life'. The fusion: authenticity (A) is what makes the sheaf's sections honest and specifically yours, while B's gluing/consistency condition is the formal version of A's self-examination — a good life is a global section, locally authored by the agent and globally non-contradictory.
contradictions: One system vs. many: B asserts 'nine principles that fit together into one coherent whole' and its final step is 'the global section exists: all parts glue' (a single, sufficient system for the good life); A is explicitly pluralistic — 'There's no wrong answer. Each response reflects a legitimate philosophical tradition… the goal isn't to pick the right philosophy' — and denies any single right philosophy.

Created vs. verified meaning: A's dominant existentialist strand holds life has no pre-given meaning and you must create it (Sartre's 'condemned to be free', Camus' Absurd); B treats the good life as a determinate, provable structure (good_life := nonharming ∧ mindful ∧ … ∧ growing) with a machine-checkable consistency theorem ('no internal contradiction').

How you know it is right: A grounds right/wrong in first-person resonance (the Life Simulator 'reveals which tradition guides your instincts', Mood Rx 'for how you feel right now', the Builder 'matches your worldview') with no external correctness condition; B grounds it in machine-checkable proof (Coq, 14 theorems, a Verify button) — the test is whether it type-checks/glues, not whether it feels right.
resolution: They operate at different levels and compose rather than cancel: A's pluralism is about which master tradition/soul-orientation you choose, while B's monism is about the small set of local principles that hold in every life regardless of tradition — and A's own six 'dominant philosophies' all converge on B's same concrete steps (which B documents as cross-cultural convergence), so 'choose your tradition for the soul (A), live the nine for the hands (B)'. A's felt authenticity supplies the CONTENT of the sheaf's sections (yours to author — 'Know YOUR limits'); B's theorems supply the SHAPE (verified, non-contradictory). A's journal / Socratic Method / Existential Audit is the informal, human version of B's gluing+consistency proof ('examination = informal proof'), and B's consistency theorem answers A's Absurd by showing a non-contradictory way to be exists. Fused: structure is proved, content is lived — a good life is a global section, locally chosen by the agent and globally consistent across Self, Other, Community.
viz: Canvas 2D 'Coherence of the Examined Life': six moods (A's felt local situations) on a hexagon, each holding one of B's ethical principles tagged with its Self/Other/Community domain-set (taken verbatim from good.html's compatibility matrix). Adjacent moods overlap; an overlap glues (green) iff the two chosen principles share a life-domain, else it tears (red). The central 'Good Life' node lights gold (pulsing) iff all six overlaps glue — B's gluing theorem run on A's first-person data. Click a mood to cycle its principle; buttons: Auto-coherent, Randomize, Reset, Theme. Readout lists the tears and states whether the global section exists. Inline data only, theme-reactive, zero network fetches.
